PUBLIC SAFETY COMMISSION
  ACTION SUMMARY
  January 16, 2024, COMMISSION MEETING

Commission Members Present: Larry Giannone (Chair), Bob Olander, Karol Curtis, Patrick
Jones, Orlando Pimental, Greg Tober, Ruth Luevand
Commission Members Absent:
City Representatives: City Manager Chris Constantin, Sr. Management Analyst Anissa Livas

 ORAL COMMUNICATIONS  COMMENTS/RECOMMENDATIONS
  Cathi Began thanked the LASD for quick
  response to December calls; highlighted that
  Via Verde community action teams combined
  with extra flock camaras are working for the
  area; and she would like to see meetings with
  Homeowners’ Associations indicated that
  online meetings are a good option.

 BUSINESS ITEMS  COMMENTS/RECOMMENDATIONS
 BI.1 Approval of Minutes for November 21,  Motion by Bob Olander and seconded by
 2023 (City Manager Chris Constantin)  Patrick Jones to approve the minutes of
  November 21, 2023. (Passed 7-0).

 BI.2 Emergency Operations Plan Update (City Anissa Livas provided a brief update on the
 Manager Chris Constantin/Sr. Management  Emergency Operations Plan and went through
 Analyst)  the comments and responses to such comments
  received in advance of the meeting.

  Commissioners discussed emergency plan
  activations levels, response times, activation
  criteria, preparedness, CERT training, current
  City and partner efforts for disaster response
  preparation.
 January 16, 2024 Public Safety Commission Minutes  Page 2

  Bob Olander recommended adding terms of
  terrorism, cyber-attack into Section 2.3 given
  the significance of such potential incidents.

  Motion by Patrick Jones and seconded by Bob
  Olander to recommend the Emergency
  Operations Plan to the City Council for
  approval. (Passed 7-0).
 BI.2 Discussion of Part 1 Crimes for January  Captain Ashrafnia provided an update on part 1
 – November 2023 (Captain Walid Ashrafnia)  crime statistics from January to November
  2023 and discussed trends related to each crime
  type category.

  Ashrafnia provided an update on the recent
  murder in north San Dimas as well as the Flock
  camara system as being instrumental to
  capturing the alleged murder suspect.

  Commissions asked about the extent of fires
  that are occurring around the freeways. There
  were concerns related to the dozens of fires that
  have occurred in the last two years from
  encampments along the freeways.
 BI.4 Discussion of Fiscal Year 2024-25 Budget  City staff requested a discussion on potential
 Priorities (City Manager Chris Constantin)  budget priorities the commission desired the
  City Manager and City Council to consider in
  the 2024-25 budget.

  Patrick Jones inquired about the cost of making
  a current one-person LASD vehicle into a two-
  person vehicle. Discussion included the costs
  of such item.

  Commissioners supported the expansion of
  Flock camera systems and finding
  opportunities to free up funding to leverage
  technology, such as A.I. to enhance public
  safety.
 NEW BUSINESS ITEMS  COMMENTS/RECOMMENDATIONS
 R1 Commissioner Reports  Patrick Jones – Jones presented information
  regarding the fire risks associated with electric
  vehicles and the danger charging the vehicle in
  garages.

  Ruth Luevand – Luevand thanked staff for
  doing research into A.I.
 January 16, 2024 Public Safety Commission Minutes  Page 3

  Orlando Pimental – Pimental thanked the City
  Manager and public speaker in reference to the
  increased future use of A.I., data driven
  policing and technology.

  Bob Olander – Olander informed
  commissioners that March 5th is the City
  election for two districts and a candidates night
  on January 31st at 6pm in the Plummer
  Building.

  Karol Curtis – Curtis recognized the frighting
  impact of fires as shown in the PBS show
  “When the Smoke Clears” related to the
  Paradise fire.

  Greg Tobar – Tobar appreciated staff being
  ahead on the use of technology for public
  safety.

 R2 Station Captain’s Report (Captain  Captain Ashrafnia highlighted the status of the
 Ashrafnia)  Grants Pass case which is going to the Supreme
  Court. This is an important case related to the
  unhoused.

 R3 City Staff Liaison Report (City Manager  The City Manager updated the commission on
 Chris Constantin)  two ordinances that the City Council is
  considering. The ordinances govern who
  transit shelters can be used and the activity that
  would be restricted in public spaces. The
  importance of these and future ordinances is to
  ensure we balance the use of public spaces with
  compassion and accountability.

The meeting adjourned at 7:19 PM.
